correctness.rationale: The source treats the full downward closure of strict-filtration matching faces, not the pure or ordinary Morse complex. A cyclic word in {0,+,-} is realizable iff adjacent nonzero signs do not disagree and a monochromatic word leaves a cyclic consecutive 00; this follows because exactly nonconstant orientations of a cycle are acyclic and arise from an injective height order. The bipartite independence complex L=Ind(B_n), with each x_i adjacent to y_{i-1},y_i,y_{i+1}, captures the local condition; omitted L\K faces are purely monochromatic vertex covers. Hence integral C_*(L,K) splits into two simplex/Alexander-dual ordinary-cycle pairs. The union U of all y-vertex closed stars has every nonempty finite intersection a cone, and L=Delta_X union U with Delta_X∩U=Ind_2(C_n)^vee, so L is the suspension of that dual. Integral Alexander duality and Deshpande–Singh/Kozlov wedge types determine relative groups and L groups with degree shifts. Since d2(n)>d1(n) for all n>=6, same-degree L→H(L,K) connecting terms vanish; the resulting short exact sequences split over Z because quotient groups are free. This proves all integral groups and no torsion, including coincident resulting K degrees. Independent FROM-SCRATCH strict-height/word face checks for n=6,7,8 and separate mod-2 boundary ranks through n=9 reproduce 163,421,1061 strict faces and predicted ranks (n6: degree2 rank5; n7: degree2 rank1, degree3 rank2; n8: degree3 rank5; n9: degree4 rank5); formula evaluation at n=22 gives H10=Z,H13=Z^2. These finite checks are corroboration only, not proof of all n or integral torsion freeness.

final_claim: Let K_n be the full strong discrete Morse matching complex generated by strict vertex filtrations of the one-dimensional cycle C_n, n>=6. Let (d1,a1) be (k-1,2),(k-1,1),(k,1) at n=3k,3k+1,3k+2. Let (d2,a2) be (2k-1,3),(2k-1,1),(2k,1),(2k+1,1) at n=4k,4k+1,4k+2,4k+3. For each i>=0, reduced H_i(K_n;Z) is the direct sum of free abelian groups of rank a2 in degree i=n-2-d2 and rank 2a1 in degree i=n-3-d1, summing ranks if degrees coincide; all other groups vanish and there is no torsion. In particular at n=22 the nonzero reduced integral groups are H10=Z and H13=Z^2. No claim of a wedge decomposition or equivariant integral representation.
